Kernel subsystems move, one subsystem at a time, out of hand-written Rust models and into proven Thermite carried through the boundary registry, so the proportion of the running image that is certified rises monotonically.

```day-telos
{"witnesses":["verified-source"]}
```

Did not advance. The verified-source witness is material only because src/*.th exists, and its contents are the upstream trivial payload: one exported function whose postcondition is result > 0. No subsystem moved from hand-written Rust into proven Thermite this pass. A material witness is not an advanced telos, and this is the case that shows the difference. Blocked at T0 by upstream Thermite #122.

The meso line is drawn by invariant locality: a subsystem is admissible when its invariant is local, or can be made local by an affine ownership grant. Local invariants compose additively; cross-cutting ones compose multiplicatively over the product state space. Thermite's move semantics make grants unforgeable, verified by E0382 on reuse.

Bulla designs the composed data model and treats G4's flat type universe as an encoding with a mechanical mapping, rather than designing around it. An encoding produced by a stated rule can be re-derived when the constraint lifts; a design shaped around a limitation has to be rediscovered.

The scheduler fails the invariant-locality test as usually written — its invariant relates the runqueue to every thread's state, the multiplicative shape. It becomes admissible if runnability is an affine grant the scheduler holds. That is a design commitment that has not been tried, and it is where the locality principle produces a non-obvious verdict.

Bulla's position is a rung, not a fixed point. Each rung is a proof capability the language has or lacks; each moves a kernel affordance from 'an unverified guest provides it' to 'the verified core provides it'. That makes meso measurable and gives every gap filed a place in an order. Recorded in docs/the-ladder.md.
